q-277907.problem:
In **ascending order**, the roots of $f(t)=\frac{{t}^{2}-4t-21}{{t}^{2}+7t+10}$ are

$t=$
{{field-1}} $\,$
and
$\,\,t=$
{{field-2}}
q-277907.worked_solution:
The roots of $f(t)$ are the solutions to the equation $f(t)=0.$ In our case, we have

$$
\frac{{t}^{2}-4t-21}{{t}^{2}+7t+10}=0.
$$

First, we factor $f(t),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =\frac{{t}^{2}-4t-21}{{t}^{2}+7t+10} \\  & =\frac{(t-7)(t+3)}{(t+5)(t+2)}.\end{aligned}
$$

There are no common factors in the numerator and denominator, so we set the numerator equal to zero and solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(t-7)(t+3) & =0 \\ t & =7,\,-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions to $f(t)=0$, in ascending order, are $t=-3$ and $t=7.$

q-277916.problem:

$x=$

q-277916.worked_solution:
The roots of $f(x)$ are the solutions to the equation $f(x)=0.$ In our case, we have

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+2x-8}{{x}^{2}-9x+18}=0.
$$

First, we factor $f(x),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{{x}^{2}+2x-8}{{x}^{2}-9x+18} \\  & =\frac{(x+4)(x-2)}{(x-3)(x-6)}.\end{aligned}
$$

There are no common factors in the numerator and denominator, so we set the numerator equal to zero and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+4)(x-2) & =0 \\ x & =-4,\,2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions to $f(x)=0$, in ascending order, are $x=-4$ and $x=2.$

q-277942.name: Question 3
q-277942.worked_solution:
First, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =\frac{{t}^{2}-5t+6}{3t-9} \\  & =\frac{(t-3)(t-2)}{3(t-3)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{(t-3)}(t-2)}{3\cancel{(t-3)}} \\  & =\frac{(t-2)}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the numerator equal to zero and solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}t-2 & =0\,⟹\,t=2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to $f(t)=0$ is $t=2.$
